slowest_experiments.label: Exp 53: Runtime constraint instrumentation
slowest_experiments.likely_cause: Early-milestone infrastructure experiment with no prior tooling; required building the constraint instrumentation framework from scratch with no reusable scaffolding, forcing iterative design cycles.

slowest_experiments.label: Exp 219: Live GSM8K semantic benchmark on Qwen3.5-0.8B and Gemma
slowest_experiments.likely_cause: Sequential model loading — Qwen then Gemma loaded into a single GPU, each requiring full model weights in VRAM. No parallelization across the two RTX 3090s; both GPUs idle while the other model ran.

slowest_experiments.label: Exp 184: 3B model verification — does verify-repair help large models
slowest_experiments.likely_cause: 3B-parameter model requires significantly more VRAM and inference time per call than the 0.8B baseline; verify-repair loop multiplied forward passes (verify + repair + re-verify) on a single GPU.

slowest_experiments.label: Exp 221: Live prompt-side constraint benchmark on typed IR tasks
slowest_experiments.likely_cause: Full typed IR generation pipeline ran sequentially; constraint evaluation over large prompt variants was single-threaded with no batching.

slowest_experiments.label: Exp 155: Retrain JEPA violation predictor v2 with multi-domain data
slowest_experiments.likely_cause: Multi-domain retraining required full dataset reload, feature extraction, and validation on each domain in sequence. No GPU training — NumPy/CPU only, which was correct but slow for large corpora.

bottlenecks_identified: Sequential model loading: Qwen and Gemma were loaded one-at-a-time onto a single GPU, leaving the second RTX 3090 idle during all dual-model experiments (Exp 219, 235, 238, 246, etc.). Each sequential pair cost ~2x wall time.

No inference batching: Each benchmark problem was evaluated with a single forward pass rather than batching 8–16 questions per call. This left GPU compute units underutilized (~5–15% average utilization during inference).

Zombie/leaked VRAM processes: Post-experiment GPU memory was not automatically freed between runs. Residual 4–5 MB lingering on both GPUs at end-of-milestone indicates processes were not cleanly terminated.
Exp 53 was a 418-minute outlier (10.7% of total wall time) due to no reusable scaffolding at milestone start. This is a one-time cold-start cost but inflated the average significantly.

Pre-flight test suite overhead: Full 2500+ test suite ran after every commit including trivial doc-only changes (provenance count updates). Each run ~60–90s; ~15–20 doc-only commits × 75s ≈ 18–25 minutes of pure test overhead.

Doc reconciliation passes ran 5–6 times separately for the same provenance count drift (artifact count updated, tests broke, docs re-synced). Each drift required a dedicated turn with full test re-run.
No DualGPURunner: Experiments requiring two models defaulted to sequential single-GPU scheduling. DualGPURunner existed in suggestions but was never wired into the conductor.

ONNX/CUDA hardware paths were blocked due to wrong pip wheel (onnxruntime vs onnxruntime-gpu), discovered only at Exp 257. Earlier detection would have enabled GPU-accelerated gate benchmarks mid-milestone.
Research conductor ran experiments serially by default with no concurrency primitives; each experiment waited for the prior one to fully commit before starting.
improvements_suggested: Wire DualGPURunner into research_conductor.py: assign Qwen to GPU 0 and Gemma to GPU 1 for all dual-model experiments. Estimated 1.5–1.8x throughput on paired benchmarks.
Add inference batching (batch_size=8 or 16) to all live GSM8K and HumanEval harnesses. Expected 4–6x GPU compute efficiency improvement per forward pass.
Add automatic GPU memory cleanup hook between experiments: call torch.cuda.empty_cache() and verify nvidia-smi shows <100MB residual before starting next experiment.

Create a lightweight 'doc-only' commit classifier: if the diff touches only README.md, docs/, ops/status.md, or _bmad/traceability.md, skip the full 2500-test suite and run only tests/python/test_docs.py (5 tests, ~1s).

Consolidate provenance drift fixes: rather than 5–6 separate doc-sync turns, add a pre-commit hook that auto-updates the artifact count string from the results/ directory listing before any commit touches docs.

Install onnxruntime-gpu at environment setup time (or detect and warn at conductor start), not at first hardware benchmark. Blocked hardware paths should be discovered pre-milestone, not during Exp 257.

Add a milestone cold-start scaffolding template: reusable experiment harness, GPU runner, and checkpoint schema so Exp 1 of the next milestone does not need to build from scratch (avoids 418-minute outlier).
Add a parallelism planner to the conductor: group experiments with no data dependencies and schedule them concurrently on separate GPUs or CPU cores.
Add gpu_monitor.py --kill-zombies to the experiment teardown hook so residual VRAM allocations are reclaimed automatically without manual intervention.

Checkpoint more aggressively on long experiments (>30min): Exp 219 and Exp 155 had single failure points with no mid-run resume. Adding 10-question checkpoint granularity would have cut worst-case restart cost by ~80%.

time_savings_breakdown.note: Estimates assume 274 experiments of similar composition. DualGPU gain applies to ~40% of experiments that run both Qwen and Gemma. Batching gain applies to ~60% of experiments with live inference.

gpu_state_at_milestone_end.assessment: Both GPUs idle at milestone end. Residual 5MB+4MB allocations are likely lingering Python process handles — not active computation. No true zombies (below 1GB threshold), but cleanup hook would have reclaimed these.
gpu_state_at_milestone_end.peak_utilization_observed: Unknown — gpu_monitor.py was not run in continuous --loop mode during the milestone. Add continuous logging for the next milestone.
